title: Document all public items and enforce with #![warn(missing_docs)]
description:
A `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` shows 39 undocumented public items in src/lib.rs (7 structs, 22 struct fields, 8 methods, 2 associated functions), including the public result types (UpdateStatus, LatestReleaseInfo, UpdateOutcome, AssetNames) and several Updater methods (new, config, current_status, check_latest, stage_next, run_update) and EmptyArgs/UpdateError. For a crate that ships full crates.io publishing metadata, this leaves a sparse docs.rs page.

Add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` at the crate root and write a concise doc comment for every public item so the lint is satisfied. Because CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, this also enforces documentation on all future public items (new undocumented pub items will fail CI).

Acceptance: `RUSTFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo build` is clean (0 missing-doc warnings); cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + test (22 unit + 2 doc-tests) stay green; cargo doc --no-deps builds clean. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.

title: Make Unix-only platform support explicit; remove dead #[cfg(not(unix))] exec_replace branch
description:
Portability inconsistency in src/lib.rs.

Current state:
- Module unconditionally does `use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;` (top of lib.rs) and calls `set_mode(...)` in `set_executable` and tests. These are Unix-only APIs; `std::os::unix` does not exist on Windows, so the crate cannot compile on non-Unix targets.
- `release_target()` only maps linux->linux and macos->darwin, and bails on any other OS. So even at runtime only Linux/macOS are supported.
- Despite that, `exec_replace` has a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback (spawn + exit) alongside the `#[cfg(unix)]` `CommandExt::exec` path. Because the unconditional unix import already prevents non-unix compilation, the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` branch is unreachable/dead code and never builds.

Net: the crate is effectively Unix-only (Linux/macOS), but the dead non-unix branch and the cfg gating imply cross-platform intent that does not hold. For a reusable crate published with full crates.io metadata, this is misleading.

Recommended minimal fix (commit to Unix-only honestly):
- Remove the dead `#[cfg(not(unix))]` exec_replace fn and the now-redundant `#[cfg(unix)]` gate on the remaining definition, making exec_replace a plain Unix fn consistent with the rest of the module.
- Add an explicit "Platform support: Unix (Linux/macOS) only" note to the crate-level doc comment and the README.

Optional larger follow-up (defer unless there is demand): add real Windows support — cfg-gate the unix imports, provide a Windows set_executable no-op, and add a Windows release_target arm plus a zip-based asset strategy. Not in scope for this bead.

Acceptance: crate still builds + cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; no dead non-unix branch remains; docs/README state Unix-only support. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli (board was empty).

title: Crate is not crates.io-publishable: mcp-cli git dependency has no version (cargo publish fails)
description:
updatable-cli ships full crates.io publishing metadata (description, license, keywords, categories, repository, homepage, readme) implying it is meant to be published, but `cargo publish --dry-run` FAILS:

  error: failed to verify manifest ... all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when publishing. dependency `mcp-cli` does not specify a version

Root cause: Cargo.toml depends on `mcp-cli = { git = "https://github.com/harryaskham/mcp-cli", branch = "main" }`. crates.io rejects git/path-only dependencies; every dependency (including optional ones) must carry a semver version that exists on crates.io.

Important: feature-gating / making mcp-cli optional does NOT bypass this — optional dependencies still require a version requirement at publish time. So the crate cannot be published to crates.io until mcp-cli itself is published to crates.io.

Options considered:
1. Publish mcp-cli to crates.io, then in updatable-cli pin a version (git for dev via [patch]).
2. Decide updatable-cli is intentionally NOT crates.io-published (git-only) and relax the publishing metadata.
3. Split the MCP surface into a separate crate so the core can publish without mcp-cli.

Verified via `cargo publish --dry-run`. Discovered during overnight in-lane review (node aurora).

DECISION (2026-06-23, operator via choice-019ef688, freeform "no crates.io, just idle"): option 2 — updatable-cli is intentionally NOT published to crates.io; it is consumed git-only across the CLI suite. The "not publishable" state is BY DESIGN, not a defect, so no fix is required. Optional non-urgent follow-up if ever desired: relax the crates.io publishing metadata (keywords/categories) so it doesn't imply crates.io intent. Deferred per operator "just idle"; left as draft for the operator to discard or action at leisure.

title: Private-repo support: attach token to asset downloads + optional gh-account token source
description:
Private-repo updates are only half-wired today. `UpdaterConfig.github_token` is sent as Authorization: Bearer only on the check_latest metadata request (lib.rs:224); the actual asset/checksum downloads in stage_next go through download_bytes/download_text which set User-Agent only and never attach the token. So even a correctly-authed caller cannot download a private release asset — it 404s. Confirmed bug, not caller misuse (kittui is wiring a stopgap).

Scope:
1. Thread the resolved token into asset + checksum downloads with redirect-safe handling that strips Authorization on cross-host redirects (GitHub -> signed S3 URL) so private downloads actually work.
2. Add an opt-in convenience for callers to source a token from the local gh CLI when none is set explicitly: new UpdaterConfig fields gh_account (Option<String>) and gh_token_fallback (bool), plus a gh_auth_token(account) helper running `gh auth token [--user <account>]`. github_token still wins; gh is only invoked when gh_account is set or gh_token_fallback is true, keeping existing public-repo behaviour and tests deterministic.
3. Builder helpers with_github_token/with_gh_account/with_gh_token_fallback and resolved_token().
4. Tests: auth header present on downloads when token set; auth stripped on cross-host redirect; resolved_token prefers explicit token without invoking gh.
5. README docs for private-repo + gh-account configuration.

Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator request.

title: check_latest: friendlier errors for no-releases (404) and rate-limit (403/429)
description:
check_latest() in src/lib.rs propagates raw ureq errors instead of giving actionable messages for the two most common failure modes when polling GitHub releases:

- 404: the repo has no published releases yet (very common for a freshly set-up tool). Currently surfaces as a generic `GET <url>` ureq Status error.
- 403/429: GitHub API rate limiting (anonymous requests are limited to ~60/hr). Currently surfaces as a generic Status error with no hint that adding a token would fix it.

This is inconsistent with download_bytes(), which already maps `ureq::Error::Status(code, _)` to a clear `GET <url> returned HTTP <code>` message.

Fix: in check_latest, match on `request.call()`:
- 404 -> bail with "no published GitHub releases for <repo_slug> yet (GET <url> returned 404)"
- 403 | 429 -> bail with a message noting the request was rate-limited/forbidden and suggesting `UpdaterConfig::with_github_token` / `with_gh_token_fallback` to raise the limit
- other Status(code) -> "GET <url> returned HTTP <code>" (consistent with download_bytes)
- transport Err -> "GET <url>: <err>"

Add tests using a small std-only mock-HTTP helper that returns a custom status line (extend spawn_one_shot_http): one asserting the friendly no-releases message on 404, one asserting the rate-limit/token hint on 403.

Acceptance: cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; new tests cover 404 + 403 paths; behaviour unchanged on the success path. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli.
